desc: Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) is the primary international airport serving Delhi and the National Capital Region. It is the busiest airport in India by passenger traffic and cargo volume. The airport spans over 5,106 acres and features three operational terminals, with Terminal 3 being one of the largest airport terminals in the world. It serves as the primary hub for Air India and a major hub for IndiGo, SpiceJet, and Vistara. The airport has been consistently ranked among the world's best airports for service quality.
fact: It is the busiest airport in India by passenger traffic and cargo volume · Terminal 3 is one of the largest airport terminals in the world · It serves as the primary hub for Air India · It has been consistently ranked among the world's best airports for service quality

desc: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM) serves Mumbai, the financial capital of India. It is the second-busiest airport in India by passenger traffic. The airport operates two main terminals: Terminal 1 for domestic and Terminal 2 for both domestic and international flights. Terminal 2 is a modern facility designed to handle 40 million passengers annually. The airport is known for its single-runway operation handling over 1,000 flights daily, making it one of the highest-traffic single-runway airports in the world.
fact: It is the second-busiest airport in India by passenger traffic · Terminal 2 handles 40 million passengers annually · It is the busiest single-runway airport in the world · It serves as the primary hub for Vistara and a major hub for IndiGo

desc: Kempegowda International Airport (BLR) serves Bengaluru, the capital of Karnataka and India's technology hub. It is the third-busiest airport in India by passenger traffic. The airport features a single integrated terminal with both domestic and international operations and a second terminal (T2) recently opened in 2023. It serves as a major hub for IndiGo, Air India, and Alliance Air. The airport is known for its modern architecture, extensive use of solar power, and being one of the largest cargo hubs in the country for perishables and electronics.
fact: It is the third-busiest airport in India by passenger traffic · Terminal 2 opened in 2023 with a focus on sustainable design · It serves as a major hub for IndiGo and Air India · It is one of the largest cargo hubs for perishables and electronics

desc: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (HYD) serves Hyderabad, the capital of Telangana. It is the fourth-busiest airport in India by passenger traffic. Opened in 2008, it replaced the old Begumpet Airport and is built on a 5,500-acre greenfield site at Shamshabad. The airport features a single integrated terminal and two runways. It is known for its operational efficiency and has won multiple awards for best airport in India. It serves as a hub for IndiGo and a focus city for Air India.
fact: It is the fourth-busiest airport in India by passenger traffic · Opened in 2008 on a 5,500-acre greenfield site · It features a single integrated terminal and two runways · It has won multiple awards for best airport in India

desc: Chennai International Airport (MAA) serves Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu and a major economic hub in South India. It is the fifth-busiest airport in India and a major gateway for southern India. The airport operates two terminals: Terminal 1 for domestic and Terminal 2 for international flights. It is a major cargo hub, particularly for the automotive and electronics industries. The airport serves as a focus city for IndiGo and Air India and is a base for the Indian Air Force.
fact: It is the fifth-busiest airport in India and a major gateway for southern India · It is a major cargo hub for the automotive and electronics industries · The airport has two terminals with a combined capacity of over 23 million passengers annually · It serves as a focus city for IndiGo and Air India

n: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport
desc: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU) serves Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal. It is the sixth-busiest airport in India and the primary aviation gateway for eastern India. The airport features a single integrated terminal that handles both domestic and international operations, along with a dedicated cargo terminal. It is a major hub for Air India and a focus city for IndiGo. The airport is the eastern center of India's aviation network, connecting the northeastern states with the rest of the country.
fact: It is the sixth-busiest airport in India and the primary aviation gateway for eastern India · It features a single integrated terminal and a dedicated cargo terminal · It is a major hub for Air India · It connects the northeastern states with the rest of the country

desc: Cochin International Airport (COK) serves Kochi, the commercial capital of Kerala. It is the seventh-busiest airport in India and the first airport in the world to be fully powered by solar energy. Opened in 1999, it was built as a public-private partnership and is the first Indian airport constructed under the build-operate-transfer model. The airport features a single integrated terminal with a distinctive Kerala architectural style. It serves as a major hub for the Gulf route, handling a large volume of passenger traffic to the Middle East.
fact: It is the first airport in the world to be fully powered by solar energy · Opened in 1999 as India's first BOT airport · It features a single integrated terminal with distinctive Kerala architecture · It handles one of the highest volumes of passenger traffic to the Middle East

desc: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport (AMD) serves Ahmedabad, the largest city in Gujarat. It is the eighth-busiest airport in India. The airport features a single integrated terminal that handles both domestic and international operations. The new Terminal 2, opened in 2025, significantly expanded capacity. The airport serves as a major hub for the textile, pharmaceutical, and diamond industries of Gujarat and is a focus city for IndiGo and SpiceJet.
fact: It is the eighth-busiest airport in India and the primary airport of Gujarat · Terminal 2 opened in 2025, significantly expanding capacity · It serves the textile, pharmaceutical, and diamond industries · It is a focus city for IndiGo and SpiceJet

desc: Goa International Airport (GOI), also known as Dabolim Airport, serves Goa, India's premier beach tourism destination. It is a civil enclave operating on the INS Hansa naval airbase. The airport handles a significant volume of charter and scheduled international flights, especially during the winter tourism season. It features a single terminal handling both domestic and international traffic. The airport is supplemented by the newer Manohar International Airport at Mopa in North Goa, which opened in 2023 to relieve congestion.
fact: It is a civil enclave operating on the INS Hansa naval airbase · It handles significant charter and scheduled international traffic during the winter tourism season · It is supplemented by the newer Manohar International Airport at Mopa opened in 2023 · It is one of the busiest airports in India for international charter flights

desc: Pune Airport (PNQ), also known as Lohegaon Airport, serves Pune, the cultural and industrial capital of Maharashtra. It is a civil enclave at the Indian Air Force base in Lohegaon. The airport features a new integrated terminal building (T2) opened in 2025 for international operations. Pune is a rapidly growing aviation market driven by the city's IT, automotive, and manufacturing industries. The airport handles direct flights to several international destinations including Dubai, Singapore, and Frankfurt.

desc: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (GAU) serves Guwahati, the largest city in Northeast India. It is the primary aviation gateway for the entire northeastern region of India. The airport features a single integrated terminal handling both domestic and international flights. It connects the northeast with major Indian cities and operates flights to Southeast Asian destinations including Bangkok and Singapore. The airport serves as a hub for the Indian Air Force and handles significant cargo traffic including tea and agricultural products.
fact: It is the primary aviation gateway for the entire northeastern region of India · It operates flights to Southeast Asian destinations including Bangkok and Singapore · It handles significant cargo traffic including tea and agricultural products · The airport serves as a hub for the Indian Air Force

desc: Jaipur International Airport (JAI), also known as Sanganer Airport, serves Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan and a major tourist destination. The airport has a single terminal building with separate domestic and international sections. It handles direct flights to several international destinations including Dubai, Sharjah, and Kuala Lumpur. The airport is a key gateway for the Golden Triangle tourist circuit (Delhi-Agra-Jaipur) and has seen significant growth in passenger traffic from international charter flights.

desc: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport (LKO) serves Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh. It is one of the busiest airports in northern India. The airport features a modern integrated terminal opened in 2022 that handles both domestic and international flights. It connects Lucknow to major international destinations including Dubai, Jeddah, Riyadh, and Kuala Lumpur. The airport serves as a major hub for pilgrimage traffic to Saudi Arabia and handles significant cargo for the region's manufacturing and agricultural sectors.

desc: Biju Patnaik International Airport (BBI) serves Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha. It is the primary airport for the state of Odisha and a growing hub for eastern India. The airport features a new integrated terminal building that opened in 2019, significantly increasing passenger handling capacity. The airport operates flights to major Indian cities and international destinations including Dubai and Bangkok. It handles significant cargo traffic from the state's mineral, seafood, and textile exports.

desc: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport (NAG) serves Nagpur, the winter capital of Maharashtra and a major logistics hub in central India. The airport is located at the geographical center of India and serves as a key air cargo hub. The new integrated terminal building opened in 2022, enhancing both domestic and international connectivity. The airport handles direct international flights to Dubai and Doha and serves the MIHAN (Multi-modal International Cargo Hub and Airport at Nagpur) project, India's largest aviation cargo hub.

n: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport
desc: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport (ATQ) serves Amritsar, the spiritual center of Sikhism and a major city in Punjab. The airport features a modern integrated terminal with distinct domestic and international sections. It is a major gateway for the Sikh diaspora, handling a high volume of passenger traffic to Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Middle East. The airport operates direct flights to London, Birmingham, Toronto, Dubai, and several other international destinations. It serves the Golden Temple and the India-Pakistan Wagah border crossing.

desc: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport (VNS) serves Varanasi, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities and the spiritual capital of India. The airport features a new integrated terminal building that opened in 2019 with a design inspired by Hindu temple architecture. It connects Varanasi to major international destinations including Dubai, Bangkok, Colombo, and Kuala Lumpur. The airport handles significant pilgrimage traffic for the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and the Ganges River ghats and serves as a key gateway for Buddhist pilgrims visiting Sarnath.

desc: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport (TRV) serves the capital of Kerala and is one of the oldest airports in India. The airport operates two terminals: Terminal 1 for domestic and Terminal 2 for international flights. It is a major gateway for tourism to Kerala's southern beaches and the backwaters. The airport handles direct flights to the Middle East, Maldives, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia. It also serves as a hub for the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) headquarters located in the city.
fact: It is one of the oldest airports in India · It serves as a hub for ISRO headquarters located in Thiruvananthapuram · It handles direct flights to the Middle East, Maldives, and Southeast Asia · It is a major gateway for tourism to southern Kerala

desc: Calicut International Airport (CCJ), also known as Karipur Airport, serves Kozhikode (Calicut) in northern Kerala. The airport is located on a hilltop at Karipur and features a single integrated terminal. It is one of the busiest airports in India for international traffic relative to its size, handling enormous passenger volumes to the Middle East driven by the large Malayali diaspora. The airport operates direct flights to Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Doha, Riyadh, Jeddah, Muscat, and Bahrain. It serves the Malabar region's trade in spices, textiles, and marine products.

desc: Mangalore International Airport (IXE) serves Mangalore, the port city of Karnataka. The airport is located on a hilltop at Bajpe and features a single integrated terminal. It handles direct international flights to the Middle East including Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, and Kuwait, serving the large Konkani and Tulu-speaking diaspora. The airport is built on a tabletop plateau and has one of the longest runways in Karnataka. It serves the coastal Karnataka region's trade in coffee, cashew, and marine products.
